newsitem.title: UK: FORECAST-TV ad revenue to lift Carlton H1.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST-TV ad revenue to lift Carlton H1.

text.p: Strong television advertising revenue is likely to ensure double digit pre-tax profit growth for Carlton Communcations when it releases interim figures on Wednesday.

Analysts expect pre-tax profit for the six months to end-March to climb to around 165 million pounds from 143.3 million a year ago. The dividend is likely to be increased to 4.8-5.0 pence per share, against 4.37 p.

Carlton, which operates ITV commercial television licences for London weekday television, the English Midlands and the west of England, said earlier this year that television advertising revenue had performed strongly in the first quarter.
The television division will be boosted by a maiden contribution from Westcountry TV, acquired last December.
There will also be a full six-month contribution from Carlton Screen Advertising, the cinema sales house bought last July.

Chairman Michael Green told the company's annual meeting in February that the Technicolor video duplication business had made a slow start to the year but that volumes for the year as a whole should show an improvement on 1996.
The products division is again expected to register strong profit growth as demand continues for the unit's Quantel graphics and special effects.
Analysts are awaiting news on whether Carlton and its partners in British Digital Broadcasting (BDB) have been awarded key digital terrestrial TV licences in the UK.

Carlton, Granada and BSkyB have joined forces on BDB to bid for the licences, which would allow them to offer some 15 subscription channels. They face competition from Digital Television Network (DTN), owned by Nasdaq-listed NTL Inc.
The Independent Television Commission is expected to announce the winner of the licences in the next few weeks.
